factory.discarded: Whole1 had active fire and baked wheels. Whole2 still required full cabinet/feed treatment. Native initial individual east/west corners too costly; complete west corner mirrored under diffuse light for exact reuse, no tile replacement.

decisions.source_to_native: Dimensions are not a scaled postcard: singular workshop/gantry/gate and three separate industrial landmarks assembled from complete-source architecture and complete ends/materials. No repeated chopped facade thumbnails.
decisions.floor: One actual source floor sample, no checker/no texture stamps in combat field. Grain remains restricted to architectural contact gutter.
decisions.pipe_joint: Background key shared grey with pipe/cabinet cap. Preserve only actual source pixels inside known complete coupling and cap regions; no new connector painted.
decisions.depth: Cabinet and feed assemblies end y112 behind north walk boundary. Field conveyor/crate and four street props block their entire projected footprint instead of allowing an actor to stand inside background body art. Objective egg clutches retain original non-solid destruction mechanic.
decisions.states: Ten logical nests,7 rendering slots; with x spacing144 a viewport encounters at most6 nearby clutches. Complete-map preview intentionally displays all10 logical objectives. Valve full-state65tile bank unchanged.
decisions.perimeter: Purpose-authored southern wall with cap/face/footing and pipes; complete north/south corners; architectural crop bounds checked against source dimensions. No out-of-image black padding.

limitations: Native screenshots are authored previews with a scale actor, not emulator proof or HUD captures.
Final runtime must validate controller detours, objective interactions and static prop contacts at new coordinates in both NTSC/PAL.
Symmetric reuse of complete corners is acceptable under diffuse light here; not a general rule for modules with directional cast shadows.
The long street deliberately has long quiet cladding stretches between three singular landmarks; density is a design choice to review in motion.
High/low viewports naturally clip the opposite architecture; lower industrial perimeter preserves identity in factory low camera.
